Way more than you can tell about them when meeting in person that's for sure. I recently stopped talking to a friend of mine since their political ideologies were becoming unbearable. Feeling that I could have perhaps been over-reacting, I decided to check that I'd not made a mistake by looking at their post history over on Reddit (they didn't know that I know their username). I found all kinds of stuff that totally contradicted what I knew of the actual person. For example this motherfucker pleaded poverty all of the time when it turns out that they're actually loaded - really pissed me off considering the kindness I'd showed them when we hung out.

Anyway, my point being, I think on sites such as these where there is a level of anonymity that people are more likely to be open about themselves and give clues as to what they are truly like as a person as well as details about their lives.

Something about their personality. Are they argumentative for no reason, do they make stuff up when they don't know what they're talking about, are they creative or insightful. You especially get an impression of these things when corresponding with someone over an extended period.

I look out for the marks of when to stop reading what someone has written. Bad spelling is one red flag. See one spelling error and another often follows soon after. I'm still not sure of whether that's a good sign about what the rest of someone is saying is rubbish. Other marks of speaking rubbish are use of the word "a", or use of adjectives like "excellent": For example: "This is an excellent book". Don't listen to someone who says something like that. Another example: "Find a good knife to cut through the fabric." What makes a good knife - I doubt that this person will tell us!

Also emphasizing random words: "we have A LOT of wood piled up at home." This makes you sound like a ten year old lying to his friend at school.

If someone seems very eccentric online, it is a sign that they are either very young, or very old. Old people especially are known for their creative use of punctuation. Like this..........

Frenchmen have very poor English online: there's no particular error that I notice they make, other than their writing being strewn with errors and confusing wording. Germans are hard to spot - occasionally they slip up and write "oder" when they mean "or", or put "und" for "and".

Definitely agree regarding Germans - their English online and in real life is generally top notch.
